There is no max_tokens value. BashTool's timeout field is on BashRequest in lionagi/tools/code/bash.py. Its default is None, and handle_request substitutes 30000 ms (30 s) when it is None. The value is clamped to 1 to 300000 ms (5 min).

The BashTool timeout field has no max_tokens value; it is a time limit in milliseconds. The field defaults to None (lines 31-39 of lionagi/tools/code/bash.py), and handle_request uses 30000 ms (30 s) when it is unset (line 111). The value is clamped to a range of 1 to 300000 ms (5 min) (line 112).

The Anthropic messages endpoint in lionagi has no built-in default for max_tokens: its request model declares it as required (providers/anthropic/messages.py:86, `Field(..., ge=1)`). The only default I found is applied by the CLI launch path. When an Anthropic provider is launched through an API profile, cli/agent.py:1027-1030 calls kwargs.setdefault('max_tokens', _ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS), and that constant is defined at cli/agent.py:89 as 8192. So the answer is 8192 for that CLI API-launch path. I did not verify the plain-leg path built by build_chat_model, so I cannot say what that path uses.

The default max_tokens is 32768, set by `max_tokens: int = 32768` at lion1/hub/backend/anthropic.py:234 and asserted in lion1/tests/test_anthropic.py:100. The separate lionagi/providers/anthropic/messages.py:86 declares max_tokens as required with no default.

_make_api_agent_spec (lionagi/cli/agent.py:257) builds the spec in two calls. (1) Line 271: spec.coding_tools = _API_TOOL_SETS[tools], where tools is the tool-set name argument; this selects the coding tool set for the API tool loop. (2) Line 272: _wire_secure_guards(spec, cwd), imported from lionagi/agent/spec.py (defined at line 44), which is the function that wires the security guards. _wire_secure_guards registers guard_destructive on 'bash' and guard_paths(allowed_paths=[workspace_root]) on 'reader' and 'editor' in the security_pre bucket, where workspace_root is cwd or Path.cwd() if cwd is None. Before these calls, line 268 runs AgentSpec.compose(role, effort=..., tools=['coding'], system_prompt=..., cwd=...). I did not inspect the contents of _API_TOOL_SETS, so its concrete values are not stated here.

In lionagi/cli/agent.py, _make_api_agent_spec (lines 257-273) makes two calls after composing the spec. First, spec.coding_tools is set to _API_TOOL_SETS[tools] (line 271), a lookup keyed by the tools argument. Second, _wire_secure_guards(spec, cwd) is called (line 272), imported from lionagi.agent.spec (line 266), to wire the security guards. The bodies of _API_TOOL_SETS and _wire_secure_guards are not yet read.

_wire_secure_guards registers two handlers: guard_destructive (on "bash") and guard_paths (on "reader" and "editor"), all via security_pre. guard_paths is built with allowed_paths=[cwd or Path.cwd()] and registered on reader and editor. Source: lionagi/agent/spec.py lines 44-56.

_wire_secure_guards(obj, cwd) in lionagi/agent/spec.py (lines 44-56) registers two hook handlers, both in the security_pre bucket: (1) guard_destructive on the "bash" tool (spec.py:52), and (2) a path guard, guard_paths, on the "reader" and "editor" tools (spec.py:55-56). Trace of the guard_paths registration: at spec.py:53 the function computes workspace_root = str(Path(cwd) if cwd else Path.cwd()); at spec.py:54 it builds one instance with path_guard = guard_paths(allowed_paths=[workspace_root]) (guard_paths is imported from lionagi.agent.hooks at spec.py:50); and at spec.py:55-56 that same instance is registered via obj.security_pre("reader", path_guard) and obj.security_pre("editor", path_guard). The security_pre method (spec.py:31-33) appends the handler to hook_handlers["security_pre:<tool_name>"]. The function is called from AgentSpec.coding() when secure=True (spec.py:154). The reference doc docs/reference/agent-hooks.md:174-184 describes the same two guards but calls them pre-hooks; the code uses the security_pre bucket.

The default is `Path.home() / ".lionagi"` (i.e., `~/.lionagi`), expanded with `.expanduser()`, and it is overridden by the `LIONAGI_HOME` environment variable when that is set. The definition is at `lionagi/_paths.py:20`: `LIONAGI_HOME: Path = Path(os.environ.get("LIONAGI_HOME", Path.home() / ".lionagi")).expanduser()`.

`lionagi/_paths.py` derives one path constant from it at line 21: `RUNS_ROOT = LIONAGI_HOME / "runs"`. The grep output shows no constant named `RUNS_DIR` anywhere. The MCP config module imports `RUNS_ROOT`, not `RUNS_DIR`, at `lionagi/mcp/config.py:16`: `from lionagi._paths import LIONAGI_HOME, RUNS_ROOT`.

The second constant is `JOBS_DIR = LIONAGI_HOME / "mcp" / "jobs"` at `lionagi/mcp/config.py:23`. It is derived locally in the MCP config module, not in `_paths.py`.

Caveats: the grep returned 50 of 189 matches, and I have not read `lionagi/mcp/config.py` in full. The question's name `RUNS_DIR` may be a mismatch with the source; the only runs constant I can confirm is `RUNS_ROOT`. Some other modules (e.g., `lionagi/cli/_runs.py`, `lionagi/studio/services/teams.py`) import `LIONAGI_HOME` from `lionagi.utils` rather than `lionagi._paths`, so the import source is not uniform across the codebase.

LIONAGI_HOME defaults to ~/.lionagi, i.e. Path.home() / ".lionagi" with .expanduser() applied, when the LIONAGI_HOME env var is unset (lionagi/_paths.py, line 20). Import trace: lionagi/_paths.py defines LIONAGI_HOME (line 20) and RUNS_ROOT = LIONAGI_HOME / "runs" (line 21). lionagi/mcp/config.py imports LIONAGI_HOME and RUNS_ROOT from lionagi._paths (line 16). It derives two constants: RUNS_DIR = RUNS_ROOT (line 19), which resolves to ~/.lionagi/runs by default, and JOBS_DIR = LIONAGI_HOME / "mcp" / "jobs" (line 23), which resolves to ~/.lionagi/mcp/jobs by default.
